name: Private schools and school chains

problems.words: Parents pay late every month and we chase them one by one
quick_ideas: Give every family a fee account number once, so payments and reminders never need a child's name
Send this month's reminder once to a broadcast list of parent numbers given with their permission, instead of one chat per parent, so the coordinator gets her mornings back.

workzap_build.text: customer_messaging — A fee ledger by family account number that sends reminders on a set schedule every month and shows each campus head a daily defaulter count, not a list of children.

problems.ask_first: Do most parents pay by challan, wallet or cash at the counter?
problems.free_stops: The reminder sequence, its timing and the escalation rules go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many reminder chats go out before midday on one fee day, so you see the chasing load clearly.
Give one staff member one daily reminder list at a fixed time, so parent follow-up stops getting split across the office.

problems.words: Challan, JazzCash and counter cash — nobody can tell who has actually paid
quick_ideas: Ask parents to quote the family account number on every challan and wallet payment, so each deposit can be traced to a family
Match one week of bank statement against the fee register by hand, so you can see how big the gap really is.

workzap_build.text: Challan references and wallet transaction IDs would be matched to fee accounts every day across all campuses, with money that has no account, and accounts marked paid with no money, flagged each morning.

problems.ask_first: Do unmatched payments come mostly from challans, or from wallet transfers?
problems.free_stops: How the matching rules handle part payments, siblings and wrong references is kept for the document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare one day's receipt book entries with deposits and counter cash together, so you see which payment path breaks most often.
Give one cashier the job of writing every payment method in one register daily, so paid status stops being pieced together later.

problems.words: Campus heads gave discounts with no record
quick_ideas: Ask each campus head to list current concessions by family account number once, so you see the full picture
Write down which concession types the school actually allows, so anything else stands out.

workzap_build.text: Every concession goes through owner approval before it reaches the fee ledger, with a monthly report by campus.

problems.ask_first: Do the unrecorded discounts come from one campus, or from several?
problems.free_stops: The approval levels and the monthly concession report format are set out in the document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many active concessions have a written reason on file at one campus, so the missing record problem has a size.
Give one office person one concessions notebook for every approval handed over the same day, so exceptions stop spreading across desks.

problems.words: Admissions enquiries come from Instagram, WhatsApp and walk-ins and we lose track
quick_ideas: Put this season's enquiries into one list, with each parent's number only if they gave permission, so nothing sits in three places
Make one named person responsible for callbacks, so every enquiry has an owner.

workzap_build.text: Every enquiry from ads, WhatsApp, the website and walk-ins captured directly, with stage, source and follow-up reminders, plus a season-to-date view of enquiries turning into admissions per campus.

problems.ask_first: Which source brings most enquiries: Instagram, WhatsApp, or walk-ins?
problems.free_stops: The pipeline stages and follow-up timings are kept for the document.

extra_ideas.text: Count enquiries from walk-ins, calls and messages over one admissions day, so you can see where follow-up gets missed.
Keep all new admissions enquiries in one notebook with one owner per shift, so no source gets checked later than the rest.

problems.words: We ran admission ads but don't know if one admission came from them
quick_ideas: Ask every new admission family where they heard of the school, so you have a rough source count
Run each campus's next ad with its own WhatsApp number or link, so enquiries can be told apart.

workzap_build.text: Every enquiry tagged by the ad and campus that brought it, measured all season down to admissions.

problems.ask_first: Did you run the admission ads for one campus, or for all campuses?
problems.free_stops: How the links and codes are set up per ad and campus is in the document.

extra_ideas.text: Note each new enquiry source in one admissions notebook for one week, so you can compare ads against walk-ins and referrals.
Give one admissions person a fixed end-of-day source tally, so marketing discussions stop relying on impressions from scattered chats.

problems.words: Re-enrolment only becomes clear in August
quick_ideas: Ask current families once in February–March whether they are staying, leaving or unsure, so you have counts per grade early
Plan sections from confirmed counts plus the waitlist count, not from last year's numbers.

workzap_build.text: A re-enrolment tracker that updates confirmed, pending and leaving counts per grade and campus as parents reply.

problems.ask_first: Do you hear about leavers mostly in summer, or through the whole year?
problems.free_stops: How the tracker follows up on unsure families is kept for the document.

extra_ideas.text: Count current families marked staying, leaving or unsure from one class level this week, so next term uncertainty has a visible size.
Give one admin person one weekly re-enrolment list by class, so planning stops waiting for August conversations.

problems.words: The coordinator spends an hour every morning on substitutions
quick_ideas: Ask teachers to report absence to one school number by a fixed time, so cover starts early
Print each teacher's free periods for the term once, so cover can be picked at a glance.

workzap_build.text: Absences logged each morning, free periods matched right away and the cover teacher told on WhatsApp, with a count of cover load per teacher by campus.

problems.ask_first: Do teacher absences mostly come the same morning, or are they known the day before?
problems.free_stops: The cover rules and fairness balancing are set out in the document.

extra_ideas.text: Note how many substitutions are arranged after classes start on one morning, so the delay point is easy to spot.
Give one coordinator one cover list updated at the same time each afternoon, so morning substitutions start from one place.

problems.words: Report cards take two weeks because marks come in separate Excel files
quick_ideas: Agree one shared format for marks this term, so files can be combined without retyping
Keep marks on the school's own drive, not on teachers' phones, so access stays controlled.

workzap_build.text: Marks entered once by teachers and report cards created without retyping, with access limited to staff who need it.

problems.ask_first: Do the delays come mostly from late marks, or from different file formats?
problems.free_stops: The entry screens, checks and report-card layout are kept for the document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare how many mark files arrive in the agreed format versus reworked format for one report cycle, so the retyping burden is clear.
Give one academic office person one collection deadline and one handover place for mark files, so report preparation stops chasing teachers individually.

problems.words: Van routes are decided on WhatsApp and parents complain about pick-up times
quick_ideas: Write down every route with its stops and times once, so there is one agreed version
Compare seats used per van with transport fees collected this month, so gaps show up.

workzap_build.text: cash_reconciliation — A transport register of routes, seats and fees that reconciles every month, with a one-tap delay message to parents on the affected route.

problems.ask_first: Do parents complain mostly about morning pick-up, or afternoon drop-off?
problems.free_stops: How route changes and delay alerts flow to parents is set out in the document.

extra_ideas.text: Note actual departure and arrival times for one van route on one school day, so complaint patterns can be checked against reality.
Give one transport staff member one daily route notebook handed over after each run, so timing changes stop living only in chat threads.

problems.words: Canteen cash goes missing and juice and snack stock never matches
quick_ideas: Count canteen stock and cash together at closing once this week, so you know how big the gap is
Have cash handed over daily instead of weekly, so less sits uncounted.

workzap_build.text: stock_alerts — A daily canteen close comparing stock sold with cash counted, with an alert to the owner when gaps repeat.

problems.ask_first: Does the canteen gap show more in cash, or in stock?
problems.free_stops: The variance limits and alert rules are kept for the document.

extra_ideas.text: Note opening snacks, drinks and cash at one canteen once this week, so you can compare the shortfall by shift.
Give one person the closing canteen count in one notebook each day, so stock and cash stop being checked separately.

problems.words: Each campus has its own Excel, so I can't compare them
quick_ideas: Pick the five numbers you most want from every campus, so the comparison has a shape
Ask all campuses for those numbers once, on the same date, so they line up.

workzap_build.text: One owner screen updated daily with enrolment, fee collection, defaults, staff turnover and expenses per campus, side by side.

problems.ask_first: Do all campuses use the same school setup today?
problems.free_stops: Which figures feed the screen and how they are pulled from each campus is in the document.

extra_ideas.text: Write the same weekly campus figures on one page for all branches once, so differences can be compared side by side.
Give one office person a fixed weekly time to collect each campus total into one notebook, so comparisons stop waiting on separate files.

never_say: Any promise about fees recovered, admissions gained or defaulters reduced.
Anything on fee-increase legality, KHDA/ADEK/SPEA or board inspections, or curriculum; pi says "check with your regulator or lawyer".
Advice on teacher contracts, termination or visa sponsorship; pi notes the tracking problem and says "talk to your lawyer".
Any idea that asks for, stores or repeats a student's name, photo, roll number, marks, attendance, health or family details.
Help with altered marks, forged leaving certificates, unrecorded fee receipts or covert monitoring of staff or students.
Business talk after a child safety concern; pi points to 15/1122, 999 or 911 and the school's safeguarding lead.

sample_reply.person: Fees ka koi solution batayein. Har mahine coordinator ek ek parent ko WhatsApp pe yaad dilati hai aur phir bhi aadhi class late hoti hai.
sample_reply.pi:
Haan, is ko behtar kiya ja sakta hai, aur pehla qadam aasan hai.
Pehle, har family ko ek fee account number de dein, taake payment aur reminder mein kisi bachay ka naam na aaye.
Doosra, is mahine ka reminder ek dafa broadcast list pe bhejein, un parents ke numbers pe jo unhon ne ijazat se diye hain, taake coordinator ka waqt bache.
Workzap is tarah ka intezam kar sakta hai: har mahine reminders, challan aur JazzCash payments ka roz ka match, aur har campus ka defaulter count.
